text: Bus frequency level service (LOS) classification methodology used evaluate quality bus services based frequency. classification based Highway Capacity Manual (HCM) 2000 guidelines “Service Frequency LOS Urban Scheduled Transit Service” (Exhibit 27-1), implemented GTFShift::classify_frequency_los(). LOS categories range F, representing highest level service (frequent buses) F representing lowest level service (least frequent buses). Note method adaptation original method, originally classifies LOS based headway (time) frequency (number buses per hour), last one proxy. Also, mind HCM states “LOS determined destination given transit stop, since several routes may serve given stop may serve particular destination”. Applications method scenarios consider aspect.

title: Generate GTFS with OSM geometries
text: match GTFS shapes OSM routes geometries using either GTFShift::osm_shapes_match_routes() GTFShift::osm_shapes_to_routes() enables retrieval harmonized geometries GTFS network. However, OSM geometries often MULTILINESTRING objects. contrast, GTFS shapes.txt file requires sequence points define shape. GTFShift::create_shapes_from_sf() can used overcome limitation, encapsulating conversion MULTILINESTRING objects sorted LINESTRING objects generating corresponding GTFS shapes.txt structured table. Additionally, can compute cumulative distance along shape (shape_dist_traveled), optional parameter recommended routes looping inlining.

Iterative Step iteration \(k\), current segment endpoint \(e^{(k)} = E(L^{(k)})\), define remaining segment \(L \\mathcal{R}^{(k)}\): $$d_s(L) = d\!\left(e^{(k)}, S(L)\right), \qquad d_e(L) = d\!\left(e^{(k)}, E(L)\right).$$ Segments geometry equal \(L^{(k)}\) excluded. Verification Assembly Let \(L^*\) selected candidate. $$d\!\left(L^{(k)}, L^*\right) > \operatorname{len}\!\left(L^{(k)}\right) + \operatorname{len}(L^*),$$ \(L^*\) removed remaining set loop restarts. Otherwise, \(L^*\) oriented connect \(e^{(k)}\) appended ordered sequence. points provided, consecutive unvisited points \(Q\) marked visited $$d\!\left(L^{(k+1)}, Q\right) \leq \min_{J \\mathcal{R}^{(k+1)}} d(J, Q).$$ ordered segments concatenated single LINESTRING transformed back original CRS multilinestring.

text: route, matches trips' shapes OSM route relations. matching algorithm formulated follows: Let \(R\) GTFS route identifier. 1. Filtering Base Data Selection: Let \(\mathcal{O}_R = \{O_1, \dots, O_m\}\) set candidate OSM route relations matching identifier \(R\) (based gtfs_match osm_match). \(\mathcal{O}_R\) empty, route \(R\) skipped. Unless osm_stop_order_relaxed = TRUE, relation \(\mathcal{O}_R\) entry/exit stops correct order discarded. also retrieve set GTFS shapes associated route \(R\), denoted \(\mathcal{S}_R = \{S_1, \dots, S_n\}\). 2. Feature Extraction: GTFS shape \(S_i \\mathcal{S}_R\): Extract start end coordinates trips' first last stops: \(\text{init}_{GTFS, }\) \(\text{fin}_{GTFS, }\). Compute shape's total length \(L_{GTFS, }\) number stop times \(N_{stops, }\). candidate OSM route relation \(O_j \\mathcal{O}_R\): Extract coordinates first last stops/platforms: \(\text{init}_{OSM, j}\) \(\text{fin}_{OSM, j}\). Compute relation's geometry length \(L_{OSM, j}\) number stop/platform nodes \(N_{stops, j}\). 3.
